subject: Follow-up: Encryption & KMS options — Paywise (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@paywise.com>, Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@paywise.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Encryption & KMS options — Paywise (next steps)

Hi Sam / Aisha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion and glad we could walk through the integration shape. Quick recap + proposed next steps on the encryption and key management items you flagged: 

1) In-transit: Redwood enforces TLS 1.2+ for all client <-> control-plane and control-plane <-> worker traffic; we can provide a network diagram if useful.
2) At-rest: Platform storage and model caches are encrypted with AES-256 by default. For Hosted customers keys are managed by Redwood; Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-managed keys (CMEK) via cloud KMS or an external HSM gateway.
3) KMS/HSM options: attached a short doc (Redwood-KMS-Options.pdf) that maps support across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Key points:
   - Hosted API: Redwood-managed keys; limited customer-side CMEK options today.
   - Dedicated (reserved pools): supports CMEK for object storage and DB volumes; can integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS.
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we can enable HSM-backed keys for FIPS/HSM requirements.
4) Logging & PII: we can exclude or redact PII from request logs, and we support configurable retention windows for request/trace logs.

Action items / next steps:
- Sam: Confirm whether Paywise requires CMEK for production or if Redwood-managed keys are acceptable for initial pilot.
- Security team: If you can share the specific checklist items (we have one attached) we’ll map to evidence.
- Tech deep-dive: Suggest 30–45m call next week (Dylan/Dev on our side) to go over KMS topology and audit log configs.

I attached the PDF with detailed options and a simple matrix. Happy to jump on a call — proposed times below.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood-KMS-Options.pdf

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@paywise.com>

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Encryption & KMS options — Paywise (next steps)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap and the attachment. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

- For Dedicated, when you say CMEK for object storage and DB volumes, does that cover model artifact stores (S3 buckets/compatible object stores) used by the inference runtime, or is that limited to control-plane metadata? We need assurance model artifacts use our keys.
- Key rotation: do you support automated rotation and can rotation be customer-driven (i.e., we rotate in our KMS and Redwood continues to decrypt without downtime)?
- HSM: Paywise has a requirement for FIPS 140-2 level 3 for certain keys. Is there a formal HSM/partner integration and SOC attestation we can see?
- Audit logs: we want to ensure raw request payloads that may contain PII are not persisted in long-term logs; can you confirm retention controls and redaction options?

Cc'ing security@paywise.com to keep them in the loop. Can we schedule the deep dive on Tue or Wed next week? Prefer afternoon PT.

—Sam
Sam Jenkins
Sr. Cloud Security Engineer | Paywise
sam.jenkins@paywise.com

On Sun, Nov 15, 2026 at 10:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sam / Aisha,
> 
> Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion and glad we could walk through the integration shape. Quick recap + proposed next steps on the encryption and key management items you flagged: ...

Thanks for the great questions — answered inline below and looping Dylan/Dev for the technical deep-dive.

- Model artifacts: For Dedicated, CMEK can be applied to object storage that contains model artifacts and related blobs. In practice we configure access so object stores containing model artifacts are encrypted with the customer-managed key; this covers the inference runtime reads. For Hosted, model artifact KMS is currently Redwood-managed; we can discuss migration paths for an enterprise plan.
- Key rotation: We support customer-driven rotation with a short handover window and no planned downtime — our runtime will read the new key material once permissions are updated. We also support automated rotation policies if you prefer Redwood to manage rotation on your behalf.
- HSM / FIPS: We have reference integrations with HSM partners for Private deployments and Dedicated via a partner gateway; we can share partner attestations and the SOC addendum.
- Audit logs & PII: We support configurable retention windows and log redaction rules. For sensitive workloads we can configure request logging to omit request bodies and only retain headers/metadata for traceability.

Attached: Required-Evidence-Checklist.xlsx (mapping to SOC2 / KMS / HSM items) and the KMS options PDF.

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive: Tue 11/17 1:00–1:45pm PT or Wed 11/18 2:00–2:45pm PT. Please confirm and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood-KMS-Options.pdf, Required-Evidence-Checklist.xlsx

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Encryption & KMS options — Paywise (next steps)

Hi Sam — quick technical notes from our side before the call: 

- Rotation model: We implement a dual-key rollover pattern for customer-managed KMS where the new key is added to the key policy and the service rotates reads to the new key atomically. Customers can trigger rotation via their KMS API; Redwood watches key metadata and picks up the new key without service restart.
- Model artifact access: Object stores (S3/GCS) used by the runtime are mounted with least-privilege IAM roles. When using CMEK, the bucket encryption is configured with your key and access is via role-bridging so we do not hold plaintext keys.
- Auditability: We emit cryptographic key access events to the audit stream and can route audit logs to a customer-owned Splunk/Cloud Logging sink or to our secure S3 with configurable retention.
- PII in logs: We can provide a default redaction rule set (headers+trace ids only) and an allow-list approach if you need specific fields retained for debugging.

Looking forward to the deep-dive — if you confirm Tue 11/17 1pm PT I’ll prepare a short diagram of the key flow and rotation sequence.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
